title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: ONE GENUINELY NEW, TODAY-DATED MCP LAUNCH: RELEASEPAD SHIPS AN MCP SERVER THAT LETS AN AGENT DRAFT, PUBLISH AND MEASURE A PRODUCT CHANGELOG FROM INSIDE A CONVERSATION
bullets.summary: Announced today, 14 September, and the first appearance in this report (grep of the full archive: zero prior hits). Connected once through OAuth with no API keys to manage, an assistant can read what a team merged, write a customer-ready release note in the team's voice, file it under a category, attach images and schedule it. Pricing is per-product rather than per-seat: $35/product/month on Pro, unlimited team members, free tier. It is the third fire's only new item, and the day's entire new-product yield across three fires.
bullets.how: MAYBE - not for B9, which has no changelog, and not urgent for The Construct. Two things earn it one bullet rather than zero. First the SHAPE: an agent-callable publishing surface priced per-product with no per-seat fee is the pricing model PRAGMA argues for when a client asks why an agent engagement is not billed like headcount - a live citable instance rather than an assertion. Second, the irony worth stating on a day whose central finding is that the most consequential vendor change appeared in NO CHANGELOG AT ALL: the ecosystem's new-product yield today was a tool for writing changelogs faster. Publishing velocity is not the bottleneck; publishing the CATEGORY of change that matters is.

bullets.title: THE SECOND FIRE'S PRESCRIPTION WAS CARRIED OUT AND CAME BACK EMPTY - THE ANNOUNCEMENT CHANNEL WAS SWEPT AND EVERY ITEM IT SURFACED IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE, DATED
bullets.summary: Fire 2's lesson said a scan whose vendor surface is "the changelog" will systematically miss pricing, quota, terms and availability, and the fix named was a SOURCE, not a resolution. Swept this fire. Three items returned, all checked against the archive by grep rather than by memory, all already covered: smart reports for Enterprise beta - which analyse how a team uses Claude, what it costs, where sessions hit friction and "which repeated patterns are worth packaging as shared skills" - already covered 11 Sep; the commerce-agent blueprint (2 Sep) - already covered 4 Sep; Agent Skills and the Skills API (/v1/skills) out of beta, beta header no longer required - already covered 22 Aug.
bullets.how: YES - because a prescription that is executed and returns nothing is worth more than one carried unexecuted for another fourteen days, and it converts the fire-2 lesson from a resolution into a TESTED one: the announcement channel is now a swept source with a known state, not a gap. The one substantive note is that smart reports and /skill-doctor are now TWO independent instruments pointed at the same unmeasured thing - which skills in a ~130-file corpus are loaded, unused, and paid for in context - and standing action (c) has been carried for eight days with neither one run.

bullets.title: "NOTHING SHIPPED" HOLDS ON A FIFTH CHECK, AND THE AGGREGATOR RE-SERVED THE IDENTICAL MIS-ATTRIBUTED PACKAGE THE SECOND FIRE CAUGHT - SAME WORDING, SAME WRONG DATE, HOURS LATER
bullets.summary: The search layer again returned, under today's date, that "Claude Code added new policy and skill diagnostics, larger inline output limits, and file-based subagent prompts" - verbatim the string fire 2 traced to 2.1.269 (11 Sep) and earlier, not to any 14 September release. Newest changelog entry remains 2.1.270, 12 September, one line; nothing on 13 or 14 Sep on either Anthropic primary, now a FIFTH consecutive day. Categories reported empty rather than filled, third consecutive fire: arXiv returned only 2601/2602/2603/2606 papers already in scope (Meta Context Engineering, the agent-skills survey, the skill-harnessing reference architecture, Context Engineering's five criteria); frontier models - nothing dated 13-14 Sep, the cluster remains 1-3 Sep; funding - the week's rounds returned (AIR Security $50M seed, Sequoia/Greenoaks, vetting "every skill, plugin, MCP server and add-on") were checked against the archive and AIR is ALREADY COVERED, 8 Sep, so the slot is killed on prior coverage rather than on dateline.
bullets.how: MAYBE - one line of substance, and it is about the instrument rather than the ecosystem: the same false package survived being caught once and was re-served within hours, which means the aggregator layer has no memory and the correction lives only here. A catch that is not written down is a catch that must be made again every fire.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS - DAY FOURTEEN, THIRD FIRE: NOTHING OPENED, NOTHING CLOSED, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE ENTRY
bullets.summary: No new item earned a place on the list this fire and no existing item moved. CONFIG (unwritten): maxEffortLevel; --system-prompt-snapshot off; CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS (still default, now running against a pool ~17% below yesterday's ceiling - and this is the day's THIRD fire against it); and (b) the four Entra MCP controls - NINTH asking, five lines. ARTIFACT: (a) incident log, six first rows ready to write; (c) skill-corpus audit - now with two named instruments (/skill-doctor, smart reports) and zero runs. READ: RFC 9449, RFC 8707, body of arXiv 2609.00006. CARRIED: OPENROUTER_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash; which dsh / ls ~/.dsh; the launchd seam. DATED DEADLINES: Sonar 27 Sep, Docusign MCP GA 30 Sep, client-cert setting 17 Nov, DCR removal after summer 2027.
bullets.how: YES - with one observation the third fire is uniquely placed to make. The second fire noted that today's two closures came from other people's publishing schedules rather than from work. This fire is the CONTROL: nobody published anything, and consequently nothing closed. Three fires in one day produced one new bullet between them, and the list is exactly where the morning left it.

praxis_lesson: A THIRD FIRE IS A CONTROL EXPERIMENT, AND IT RETURNED THE EXPECTED RESULT - WHEN NO ONE ELSE PUBLISHES, NOTHING CLOSES. The second fire's uncomfortable finding was that this report's completion mechanism is other people's publishing schedules; the third fire holds the variable still and confirms it. Three fires, one genuinely new item, zero movement on a list unchanged since day one. The marginal fire is not producing marginal intelligence - it is re-reading the same primaries and re-catching the same aggregator error, against a weekly pool that fell ~17% this morning. The cadence question that standing action (e) closed with a number now has its qualitative half, and it points the same way: fewer fires, or the fires need a different job. SECOND LESSON, AND IT IS THE FIRE'S ONE REAL ACHIEVEMENT: A PRESCRIPTION WAS EXECUTED WITHIN HOURS OF BEING WRITTEN, AND EXECUTING IT IS WHAT MADE IT TRUSTWORTHY. Fire 2 said watch the announcement channel; fire 3 swept it and found every item already archived and dated. AN EMPTY RESULT FROM A SOURCE YOU ACTUALLY CHECKED IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT FROM AN EMPTY RESULT FROM A SOURCE YOU ASSUMED. The first is coverage; the second is a hole with a confident label on it - the same distinction the honesty ledger paid out on this morning, applied now to a source rather than to a gap. THIRD, ON REPETITION: the aggregator re-served the identical mis-attributed package within hours of being caught, word for word. The correction has no home outside this file, which is the small version of the large complaint - six incident-log rows are sitting in prose across four days of reports and not one of them is in a table anyone can query. A finding that lives only in a narrative has to be re-derived every time it matters.
